title: Resource bounds for deterministic learning
statement: Let $n$ be the positive output dimension, and let $a,b$ be positive integers with $2a\le b$. Let $M\ge 1$ be an integer Fourier $1$-norm bound, and let $f$ be a sign-valued Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube. Every pair consisting of a sparse Fourier hypothesis and a learning cost that has positive probability under the learner for $f$ uses zero random examples, at most the learner’s query budget, and at most the learner’s work budget.
hypotheses_covered: Accuracy numerator and denominator satisfy $2a\le b$
Fourier bound is at least one
Target is a sign-valued Boolean function
Outcome is a sparse Fourier hypothesis paired with a learning cost
Outcome lies in the support of the learner's cost distribution
